dedupe_keys.name: nova scotia waste to energy technology selection and capacity planning in a multi facility system

description: This case study plans where to build waste-to-energy facilities in Nova Scotia, Canada, which technologies to install and how to distribute their energy. Ahmed Saif and Khaled Zoroufchi Benis of Dalhousie University built a strategic optimisation model that locates processing facilities, assigns waste-generating communities to them, chooses equipment types and capacities, and routes electricity, heat and hydrogen to demand points, with two objectives: maximising profit and minimising greenhouse gas emissions. They derived cost, emission and conversion functions for three technology options so they could be built into the model. The article was published in Discover Energy in June 2026 and is free to read online under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Coverage is the province, using realistic data. Caveats: the model code is not stated to be released, and results depend on assumed energy prices. The authors found that the best technology and locations depend on the objective, the cost structures and energy prices: plasma arc gasification with hydrogen separation is the most profitable because of the value of hydrogen, anaerobic digestion with combined heat and power has the lowest carbon footprint, and the optimal system is sensitive to the price of hydrogen. Simulation uses: facility location and technology choice for regional waste treatment capacity planning. Related records: the WESyS waste-to-energy simulation (model-wesys-waste-to-energy-system-simulation-p02979) addresses waste-to-energy systems with a simulation model.
